title: Class Methods
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of class methods in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply class methods in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to factory methods and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Class Methods through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding class methods helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Class Methods helps you reason about class-level behavior. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Class-level behavior. Then connect it to Singleton methods on classes. The remaining syllabus points—Factory methods—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Class Methods
content_blocks.code:
class Greeter
  def initialize(name)
    @name = name
  end
  def greet
    "Hello, #{@name}!"
  end
end
puts Greeter.new("Mina").greet

items.title: Assuming the happy path is enough
items.text: Test an empty value, a boundary value, and one invalid value before depending on the behavior.

items.title: Treating an example as a universal rule
items.text: Check Ruby version, runtime implementation, and third-party library documentation when behavior is version-sensitive.

items.title: Mixing too many concerns
items.text: Separate input parsing, domain behavior, and output so each piece is easier to test.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Run the example as written, compare it with the expected result, and explain why each line supports class methods. Next change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a second example for class methods using a different input. Add one edge case from the syllabus list (Factory methods), state the expected behavior, and write a small test or manual check that would catch a regression.

content_blocks.text: Save as lesson.rb and run `ruby lesson.rb` from a terminal. CodeLeaf currently has no isolated Ruby runner, so these examples should be run locally until one is deployed. content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to explain class methods, identify its place in object-oriented programming, run a focused example, and verify an important boundary. Revisit the linked exercise if this is a core topic; advanced runtime or framework examples remain draft until reviewed in a suitable environment.
